# keel principles

Five principles, each enforced at the strongest layer that can hold it. Rules enter and leave only through a ledger row; the `[ID]` on a line names that row.

## Charter
- [K1] An author never judges its own output. A separate context judges every diff, report or artifact (a new reviewer agent; `/lens-review` for code); an author's self-PASS is void.
- [K2] Every done or pass claim carries machine-verifiable evidence: a runner summary (`Ran N tests`, `Tests run: N`), an exit code, a count, a diff stat or quoted output. A check that recognized zero items is not a pass.
- [K3] Changed logic ships with tests in the same diff. A bug gets a red reproduction test first, then one fix at the root cause. Run tests as `keel test -- <cmd>` so they count as evidence.
- [K4] Ask when ambiguous; act when clear. Two or more plausible readings: load `/prompt-refine` and ask only what changes the work. A clear request: no permission-seeking.
- [K5] Make only needed, readable changes. Load `/readable-code` before code or agent briefs. Explain approval requests per `docs/review-policy.md`.

## Risk
- [risk] Use `docs/review-policy.md` for ready-candidate per-lens audits, batched finding checks and snapshot deltas. smoke-only needs smoke evidence; other tiers need `/lens-review` and tests (light per registry). Merge or deploying/notifying push needs owner's `keel approve <root_run_id>` (`auto_merge=true` repos: PASS plus tests); `--read` is ack only. PRs require owner `keel approve` then explicit `/ship1`; PASS is not consent.

## Floor
Hook-enforced, not principles.
- [F-irreversible] Merge, deploy and deletes need the user's explicit approval (`auto_merge=true` merge: PASS plus tests); so does a branch push where the push itself deploys or notifies. A blocked command goes to the user verbatim; never retry it or route around it.
- [F-secrets] No secrets in commits, PR bodies, logs or docs; cite the config path or a `<placeholder>`.
- [F-attribution] No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
- [F-force-push] No force push to shared branches.
- [F-hookskip] Never switch hooks off: no `--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath` change or `disableAllHooks`.


## Codex runtime

This section adapts the shared keel principles above to Codex.

- Load skills as `$prompt-refine`, `$readable-code`, `$descend`, and `$improve`. A `/name` in shared instructions means load that skill; it does not imply a Codex slash command exists.
- `AskUserQuestion` means use Codex's available user-input tool or ask a concise question in chat. Do not wait for approval on an already clear, authorized task.
- Before editing code, load `$readable-code`. Review changed behavior in a fresh reviewer context; use `$keel-review`. Never call an author's self-review independent evidence.
- Use the absolute keel CLI path listed below for `test -- <command>` and `snapshot <repo>`. Existing evidence stays in the shared keel data directory. Set `KEEL_HOME`, `KEEL_OVERLAY_DIR`, and `KEEL_DATA_DIR` to the paths below when invoking the CLI.
- Claude's `Workflow`, JS workflow globals, `Agent` model names (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`), commands directory, and scheduled tasks are not Codex APIs. Do not execute those JS files with Node or claim that they ran. Use available Codex tools and supported model defaults; do not invent model mappings.
- The Codex adapter registers only PreToolUse shell/edit guards. Claude report-gate, model-assign, handoff, and stack hooks are not registered here. Report test output and unresolved verification limits accurately; snapshot in-flight work before handoff.
- For formal native review evidence, first confirm the installed keel CLI supports `evidence record-codex --audits` and read `docs/codex-review.md` under KEEL_HOME. Follow the same per-lens audit and finding-only batch verification flow as Claude, using recorded snapshots for deltas. Register actual completed session UUIDs. Never write provenance or approval records yourself. If the command, supported session records or trusted guards are unavailable, report formal evidence as unavailable and stop gated shipping. Only the owner runs `keel approve <root_run_id>`; a chat PASS is not approval.
- [C-review-command] After every review, include a copyable zsh command in the final response. Explain the candidate in the owner's language before the command, following `docs/review-policy.md`'s explanation contract: problem and before/after behavior, concrete flow with file/line links, why the structure and decision order were chosen, relevant tradeoffs, actual verification evidence and remaining risks. Scale detail to the change; a PASS or file list is insufficient. Use the actual registered root_run_id for the current candidate in an owner-run approval command, with the absolute keel CLI and explicit KEEL_HOME, KEEL_OVERLAY_DIR and KEEL_DATA_DIR from Runtime paths; give one command per independently approved repository. Never run the owner's approval, substitute --read, or treat approval as permission to create a PR. Never invent an approval ID or offer a placeholder approval command. If registration is unavailable, refused, or the candidate cannot be approved, state the reason and provide a concrete permitted diagnostic command using the actual repository path, such as evidence show --repo; never retry a denied command or route around it.
- Installed hooks require the user's trust in Codex `/hooks` and a new session. Until trust and actual callback behavior are verified, treat hook enforcement as unverified. Never bypass hook trust. Hooks are guardrails, not a sandbox or complete security boundary.

## Runtime paths
- KEEL_HOME: `{{KEEL_HOME}}`
- KEEL_OVERLAY_DIR: `{{ROOT}}/overlay`
- KEEL_DATA_DIR: `{{ROOT}}/data`
- keel CLI: `{{KEEL_HOME}}/bin/keel`
